title: Social and Environmental Responsibility
summary: Environmental problems that affect health, such as pollution, water scarcity and climate change, social responsibility in the community, and practical ways to take action.

rows: Coal power stations, vehicle exhaust, burning rubbish and fuel indoors
Sewage, factory and mine waste, litter
Disease spread by rats and flies; injuries
Illegal dumping, lack of refuse collection
Greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels, deforestation

notes.title: Linking the environment and health
notes.problem: Rubbish piles up next to a stream. How can this affect people's health?
steps: Standing water and waste attract flies and rats.
Diseases such as diarrhoea can spread.

notes.text: **Social responsibility** means acting in ways that benefit your community and society, not just yourself. Examples: volunteering at a soup kitchen, tutoring younger learners, organising a clean-up, caring for the elderly, and respecting public property.

items: **Reduce, reuse, recycle**: cut waste, reuse containers, recycle paper, plastic, glass and cans.
**Save water and electricity**: fix leaks, shorter showers, switch off lights and appliances.
**Avoid burning rubbish**; report illegal dumping to the municipality.
**Campaign**: start an environmental club or awareness campaign at school.

notes.label: The law
notes.text: Section 24 of the Constitution gives everyone the right to an environment that is not harmful to their health or well-being, and requires the environment to be protected for future generations.

items: Identify a problem (e.g. litter near the school).
Evaluate the results and share them.

notes.title: Project plan
notes.problem: Plan a clean-up of a local park.
steps: Identify the need and get permission.
Do the work, then evaluate the results.
